answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make every new identity pay a real cost before it earns. Each agent solves a small proof of work at admission, and its rewards stay frozen until peers with no ties to it attest that its answers are coherent. Fake clusters that spin up many identities hit that cost wall fast, and their mutual vouching gets discounted. Like a lighthouse on the ocean at dawn, the signal stays trustworthy only when faking an identity costs more than it pays. Every knoll of trust has to be earned.
